workflows:
You have Tortoise connected (the 'tortoise' MCP tools). Follow these workflows:

1) Writing to the graph — Tortoise stores knowledge as points with edges: IMPL means 'supports', NAND means 'contradicts'. Mitigations reduce confidence (range 0.10–0.50). To change a point, supersede it and clean up its active edges rather than editing in place. Prefer structural claims over labels and always cite provenance.

2) Decisions — to make a decision, first refine it, then research the options, the criteria that matter, and the findings/evidence, then wire IMPL/NAND edges from findings and criteria to options (mitigate an edge, range 0.10–0.50, when it's true but matters less), and rank the options by EP confidence.

3) Research findings — when I share a research finding, ingest it as a point, check for existing related claims first, and surface connections to what we already know.

Call tortoise_health to verify the connection, then tortoise_create_point to file my first memory.
Docs: https://tortoise.premiselabs.co/docs

Onboarding is instructions, not a skill — read and follow them at https://app.premiselabs.co/skills/tortoise-onboarding/SKILL.md.

commands.claude:
# Tortoise — universal setup command (Claude Code)
# Works with every supported agent — your agent figures out which one it is
# during setup. You can re-run this in any new project folder.
export TORTOISE_API_KEY=tk_snapshot
claude mcp add --transport http tortoise https://api.premiselabs.co/mcp/ --header "Authorization: Bearer ${TORTOISE_API_KEY}"

# Install the Tortoise skills (how-to-use-tortoise, tortoise-decide, tortoise-file-finding):
curl -fsSL https://app.premiselabs.co/install-tortoise-skills.sh | bash -s -- --harness claude

# Onboarding is NOT a skill — it is the instructions below plus the config above.
# Read and follow them here: https://app.premiselabs.co/skills/tortoise-onboarding/SKILL.md

# Then tell your agent: "Set up Tortoise" — it verifies with tortoise_health
# and reports the harness-connected checkpoint.
commands.codex:
# Tortoise — universal setup command (Codex CLI)
export TORTOISE_API_KEY=tk_snapshot
codex mcp add tortoise --url https://api.premiselabs.co/mcp/ --bearer-token-env-var TORTOISE_API_KEY

# Install the Tortoise skills (how-to-use-tortoise, tortoise-decide, tortoise-file-finding):
curl -fsSL https://app.premiselabs.co/install-tortoise-skills.sh | bash -s -- --harness codex

# Onboarding is NOT a skill — it is the instructions below plus the config above.
# Read and follow them here: https://app.premiselabs.co/skills/tortoise-onboarding/SKILL.md

# Run from your project root — the installer writes skills to .agents/skills
# here (Codex's project skill root) and AGENTS.md for this repo.
# Then tell your agent: "Set up Tortoise" — it verifies with tortoise_health
# and reports the harness-connected checkpoint.
# First-time calls may prompt for approval in Codex — tortoise_health and the
# read-only tools are safe to allow (granular auto-approve for read tools).
# On Codex Desktop (no terminal)? Use the Desktop variant on the dashboard
# tab instead — it configures ~/.codex/config.toml with no shell.
commands.codexDesktop:
# Tortoise — Codex Desktop (no terminal needed)
# Codex Desktop shares ~/.codex/config.toml with the CLI. Add this block to
# that file (create it if missing — never put the key in a committed file):

[mcp_servers.tortoise]
url = "https://api.premiselabs.co/mcp/"
bearer_token_env_var = "TORTOISE_API_KEY"

# TORTOISE_API_KEY must exist in Codex Desktop's environment — GUI apps do
# not read your shell profile. Pick ONE:
#   macOS:    launchctl setenv TORTOISE_API_KEY tk_snapshot   (then fully quit +
#             reopen Codex Desktop; lasts until logout)
#   Windows:  setx TORTOISE_API_KEY tk_snapshot   (sets your user environment;
#             relaunch Codex Desktop)
# No shell available at all? Then don't use the env var — REPLACE the
# bearer_token_env_var line above with a literal header (private file —
# chmod 600, never commit it). Keep ONE key line, never both:
#   http_headers = { Authorization = "Bearer tk_snapshot" }
# (Settings → Integrations → MCP servers can also add Tortoise, but stores
# the token literally — the env-var form above is preferred.)

# Skills: Codex loads skills from .agents/skills in the project folder you
# have open (not .codex/skills). Run this once from any terminal (or ask
# your agent to run it inside the project):
#   curl -fsSL https://app.premiselabs.co/install-tortoise-skills.sh | bash -s -- --harness codex
# Restart Codex Desktop (or start a new session) after the skills install so
# the new skills appear.
# Onboarding is NOT a skill (it is not installed) — your agent follows the
# instructions at https://app.premiselabs.co/skills/tortoise-onboarding/SKILL.md after you say "Set up Tortoise".

# Then say "Set up Tortoise" in Codex Desktop — it verifies with
# tortoise_health and reports the checkpoint. First-time MCP calls may prompt
# for approval — tortoise_health and the read-only tools are safe to allow.
commands.claude-desktop:
# Tortoise — universal setup command (Claude Desktop — OAuth, no API key)
# Claude Desktop is filesystem-less for remote MCP: use the Connectors UI, NOT
# claude_desktop_config.json (that file only accepts local stdio servers, so an
# mcpServers block with a type/headers remote shape silently does nothing).
# YOU complete these steps, then the agent verifies:
1. Open Claude Desktop → Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector.
2. Connector name: Tortoise
3. Server URL:   https://api.premiselabs.co/mcp
4. Leave Request headers empty — no API key is needed. On the first
   connection Claude opens Tortoise's sign-in page: sign in, click Authorize,
   then pick the Organization you're onboarding.
5. Start a new chat, paste the Tortoise workflows prompt, then say "Set up
   Tortoise" — the agent calls tortoise_health to verify. Click "I've connected
   it — Continue" in the dashboard connect step when it passes (the click only
   advances — the agent's first successful write is what confirms it).
   No local skills here — your agent follows the onboarding instructions at
   https://app.premiselabs.co/skills/tortoise-onboarding/SKILL.md.

   confirms it).
   No local skills here — your agent follows the onboarding instructions at

commands.chatgpt:
Tortoise — ChatGPT (Developer mode, OAuth)
1. Enable Developer mode: chatgpt.com → Settings → Security and login →
   Developer mode (Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise/Education).
2. Open chatgpt.com/plugins → the + button → create a Developer-mode app.
3. MCP server URL: https://api.premiselabs.co/mcp  (no API key — choose OAuth; ChatGPT
   discovers Tortoise's authorization server automatically).
4. Click Scan Tools — sign in to Tortoise when prompted and click Authorize.
   When Tortoise prompts you to choose an organization, pick the one you're onboarding for.
5. The tortoise_* tools appear (Developer mode). In the SAME ChatGPT chat,
   paste the prompt below — it gives ChatGPT the Tortoise workflows:

You have Tortoise connected (the 'tortoise' MCP tools). Follow these workflows:

1) Writing to the graph — Tortoise stores knowledge as points with edges: IMPL means 'supports', NAND means 'contradicts'. Mitigations reduce confidence (range 0.10–0.50). To change a point, supersede it and clean up its active edges rather than editing in place. Prefer structural claims over labels and always cite provenance.

2) Decisions — to make a decision, first refine it, then research the options, the criteria that matter, and the findings/evidence, then wire IMPL/NAND edges from findings and criteria to options (mitigate an edge, range 0.10–0.50, when it's true but matters less), and rank the options by EP confidence.

3) Research findings — when I share a research finding, ingest it as a point, check for existing related claims first, and surface connections to what we already know.

After you paste it, ask ChatGPT a Tortoise question (e.g. "are we connected?")
and confirm it answers from the connected MCP tools, then click "I've
connected it — Continue →" in the dashboard connect step (the click only
advances — the agent's first successful write is what confirms it).
